newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy puts its southern ports on Albania alert.
newsitem.headline: Italy puts its southern ports on Albania alert.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Sunday Italy had sought a European Union meeting on Albania, where a state of emergency has been declared.

Dini said he had asked the Dutch, who hold the rotating EU presidency, to arrange a meeting of foreign ministry political directors either "tomorrow or at the latest the day after" to assess the situation.
The Interior Ministry put coastguards and police in Italy's southeastern ports on a state of alert for a possible rise in illegal immigrants from Albania.

Italy, which briefly occupied Albania during World War Two, is only a short distance across the Adriatic from the small Balkan country and an increasing number of illegal immigrants have arrived since Stalinist rule collapsed there.
Police in the southern city of Bari said the situation was normal and poor weather conditions were likely to have confined most small boats to harbour.
"I hope that the acts of violence and the rebellion that we have seen do not cause further migratory waves," Dini told reporters. "We must stay alert because we cannot accept illegal flows."

He said he wanted international financial organisations and the United States to take action. "A financial rescue plan has to be drawn up as soon as possible, then political action is needed," he said.
"On the latter level, we must appeal to all the forces present in Albania , both the government and the opposition, to unite, open a dialogue and respect democratic principles."

The Albanian opposition called on Sunday for an urgent meeting with President Sali Berisha on the crisis after armed rioters went on a rampage in the Adriatic town of Sarande, looting shops and setting fire to buildings.
Berisha, who spoke by telephone with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Sunday, removed the right-wing government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi on Saturday.
The crisis was triggered by the collapse of a string of risky, high-yield pyramid investment schemes in January that deprived Albanians of their savings.
The European Union has recommended that the Albanian authorities should quickly call in international experts to help them to identify measures to clean up the financial sector.
International Monetary Fund (IMF) sources said on Saturday that the IMF would send a mission to Albania in the second week of March to discuss the possibility of setting up a new loan programme.
The Foreign Ministry in Rome warned Italians not to visit Albania unless it was absolutely necessary.
The Catholic Caritas charity agency in the southern port of Brindisi called on the government and local authorities to prepare for the possible arrival of immigrants.
